G. Isolating a Failing Circuit If one of the 137004001 chips CID2, £2, FIM2, or J2 has a bad signature, there is a chance it will cause the other 137004.001 chips to have bad signatures also. If this is the case, make sure all input signatures (AO-A19, EDB0-EDB7 and CLK) are correct. If they are cor: rect, replace the 137004001 chips. If replacing the 137004-001 chips doesn't fix the problem, check for shorted or open traces in the area

If you find an incorrect signature, find the signature test point of the Math Box Circuitry on Sheet 3, Side B. Locate the IC from which the signature is being output. Check all inputs of that IC. {Hall input signatures are correct: Remove the Auxillary PCB from the circuit. Check the circuit traces common to the falling IC pin on ‘both the top and bottom of the PCB for shorts to another circuit trace. Ifthe circuit traces are not shorted, then replace the falling IC.

It an input signature is incorrect: Locate on the schematic the IC ‘source ofthe falling signature. Check the input signatures of that IC. it all input signatures are correct, then that is the failing IC. If this IC has a failing input signature, then continue “upstream in the circult flow until the failing IC is isolated.
